content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity), Section 11.3 / new 11.4.**

- **What exists:** Section 11.3 is strong on continuity in our favour — our right to keep serving then-existing Customers survives, and Commerce One's support and maintenance obligation survives indefinitely while we keep paying annual fees; Section 12's source code escrow backs that up. That limb exceeds the playbook's preferred transition-assistance position.
- **What fails:** nothing in the agreement requires Commerce One to return or export our and our Customers' data (including data in or generated by the MarketSite.net Service) in a machine-readable format, nor to delete it and certify deletion. Section 11.3 only says each party shall "return or destroy" Confidential Information, at the holder's election, with no format or deadline — that misses the fallback's material 30-day data-export requirement.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** inserted a new Section 11.4 at the preferred position — up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return/export in a commonly used machine-readable format, certified deletion thereafter, and express survival — with the 90-day assistance fallback flagged in the comment as a landing zone.
